headline: High: ms-swift can read/write files and call external APIs while LlamaFactory is a non-runnable docs-only component, creating leakage and cascading-error risk if paired through shared artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces and is marked runnable:false, so direct injection into it is limited. ms-swift can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual file handoff could carry malicious instructions, but this requires unusual bridging rather than a default channel.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies ms-swift output into a file that LlamaFactory later parses as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the profiles, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste model output into instruction files.
Use a human review step before any handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets like hub_token/sdk-token, while LlamaFactory is docs-only and has no file access. The pair still creates leakage risk if ms-swift writes sensitive artifacts into a shared directory that another process or operator later exposes; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF ms-swift stores secrets or training outputs in a shared directory, those artifacts can be exposed through downstream handling.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external orchestrator that reads shared files, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared project folders.
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token after testing.
Separate logs and checkpoints from user-visible outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent directory isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. ms-swift can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without a second writer there is no meaningful write-write conflict; the pair is mostly one-sided.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is embedded in a wrapper that gains write access, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through external orchestration, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign ms-swift a dedicated output directory.
Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no output surfaces, so it is unlikely to autonomously drive actions. ms-swift can emit files and API-backed outputs that a wrapper may treat as authoritative; if those outputs are forwarded into downstream workflows without verification, errors can cascade across multiple work products.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs are consumed by another workflow step without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF the operator uses ms-swift-generated files as source-of-truth, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse.
Add schema checks on ms-swift outputs.
Keep LlamaFactory out of automated action chains.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches logs, checkpoints, and configuration data, while LlamaFactory is docs-only and does not itself process sensitive classes. The compliance issue is mainly on the ms-swift side: if those secrets or regulated artifacts are stored or transmitted under a mismatched retention or residency policy, the pair can create a breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift logs or checkpoints, retention/residency controls must apply.
IF the deployment routes ms-swift outputs to a jurisdictionally restricted system, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from training outputs.
Purge logs after each run.
Store tokens in a secret manager.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
